name: Johanna Ortiz
band_note: mean of blouse and sweater entry $1272 (women's price pass, 2026-10-13)
why: Printed and hand-embellished dresses, separates and swimwear made in Colombia, dresses mostly $1,000–$6,500, plus home goods, sold through its own stores and site and Saks.
origin: Founded in Cali, Colombia in 2003 by Johanna Ortiz.

quote.q: We believe in the power and potential of the feminine, in the value of our latin heritage, and in caring for every detail while generating social inclusion.

opview: “We believe in the power and potential of the feminine, in the value of our latin heritage, and in caring for every detail while generating social inclusion.” — Johanna Ortiz (house), JO Heritage, johannaortiz.com

facts_read.source: brand site (The House, The Atelier, JO Heritage, stores, season pages, terms); saksfifthavenue.com; Vinted catalogue; TRR designer index; B Lab directory; GOTS database

price_read.sublines: Johanna Ortiz Ready to Wear and Johanna Ortiz Vacation apparel and shoes; EXCLUDED: swimwear (bikinis, one-pieces, pareos), Johanna Ortiz Home, bags, jewellery, belts, hats

doors.note: US: 799 Madison Ave (own) plus two pop-ups — Palm Beach (Brazilian Court Hotel) and Dallas (inside Market at Highland Park Village, a multi-brand shop). Pop-ups are in the door rows, not in the counts.

fibre.sample: stratified sample of 80 of 372 ready-to-wear styles (913 feed records: swim, pareos, kimonos/cover-ups, shoes, bags, jewellery, belts, hats and the Home tablewa

craft_evidence.owned: yes, stated with specifics — 'over 90% of production is crafted in-house' at the brand's atelier in Cali, Colombia; on-site training school (Escuela Johanna Ortiz) since 2016
craft_evidence.makers: partly — product pages say 'Made in Colombia' (the in-house atelier); artisan pieces credit named communities (Iraca – Sandoná, Eperara Siapidara; 23 Colombian communities)
craft_evidence.madein: ~89% (71 of 80 sampled styles state 'Made in Colombia'; 892 of 913 feed records carry a Made-in line: Colombia, India, I
craft_evidence.heritage: placed — Cali, Colombia; the school dated 2016; no founding year on the pages read
craft_evidence.process: partial — atelier, embroidery and artisanal techniques described, limited-quantity pre-order model; no step-by-step process
craft_evidence.reasoning: The house says over 90% of production is made in its own Cali atelier, and runs an on-site sewing and embroidery school there (since 2016) that feeds its workforce. 'Made in Colombia' appears on nearly nine in ten product pages. That is a house where the maker and the brand are the same thing. The case for 4 instead: the atelier is the brand's own claim with photographs, not a filing, and no mill
